segments.text: Welcome to Collection One of the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers: the nineteen classical and ancient centers, X one through X nineteen. Every triangle supports a rich constellation of canonical centers. It begins with the four ancient centers of Greek geometry: the Incenter X one, the Centroid X two, the Circumcenter X three, and the Orthocenter X four, joined by the Nine-Point Center X five on the Euler line and the Symmedian Point X six on the Brocard axis.

segments.text: Across Collection One, these nineteen centers organize into three structural families: first, the Euler and Brocard spine from X one to X six; second, the Contact, Perimeter, and Feuerbach centers from X seven to X twelve — where the Gergonne, Nagel, Mittenpunkt, and Spieker points govern tangency and perimeter, and the Feuerbach pair X eleven and X twelve mark the tangency of the incircle and nine-point circle; and third, the Equilateral Six and Clawson point from X thirteen to X nineteen. Three master central lines bind the collection together: the Euler line through X two, X three, X four, and X five; the Nagel line through X one, X two, X eight, and X ten; and the Brocard axis through X three, X six, X fifteen, and X sixteen.

segments.text: Finally, three transformations — isogonal conjugation, isotomic conjugation, and centroid homothety — map these centers into one another, while erected equilateral triangles generate the Fermat points X thirteen and X fourteen, the Isodynamic points X fifteen and X sixteen, and the Napoleon points X seventeen and X eighteen, crowned by the Clawson point X nineteen.
